sections.html: A splendid large barb from Burma (Myanmar), reaching a maximum size of approx. 60 cm. The extremely large, diamond-shaped blue scales on the back shine brightly in a swimming fish, and the orange-red stripe on the side looks gorgeous. Under flash photography from the front the fish looks rather drab silvery; the colours can be shown in photos only in slightly underexposed pictures and grazing light.
Neolissochilus inhabit rivers in primary forests of subtropical regions of northern India, Burma, Thailand and most probably Cambodia.
The water in their habitats is always very clean, and the fish are known to disappear when human activities (clearing, water pollution) increase.

Due to its geographical distribution the species is adapted to water temperatures between 16 and 26°C. It is already a much sought-after fish for koi carp ponds in tropical Asia (at temperatures between 22 and 24°C).

Lexicon: Neolissochilus: ancient Greek, means "new Lissochilus"; Lissochilus is another genus of barb. stracheyi: dedication name. Blue Tor: the common name refers to the large blue scales on the back and the overall similarity of the fish to the members of the carp genus Tor.
